kata.name: Mediator interaction dispatched by a second center - both parties hold the main hub while the dispatch goes to the legacy hub
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md mediator row (disposed; discovery-only candidate); fixtures/katas/mediator/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.5
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: both coherence equations fire on the same interaction row while the per-arrow suite passes; the fault is a foreign dispatch with canonical participants (survived, scoped)

expected.detail: i_ca.dispatched_by = hub_legacy while speaker carol and listener alice both hold hub_main; eq0 (listener) and eq1 (speaker) emit executed violations on i_ca. The per-arrow sample sees only a declared dispatch row

commands: python3 prototype/mediator_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline reports no detection on this fixture
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/mediator/dispatch-second-center.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 2 violations

comparison.conventional_baseline: the frozen per-arrow suite asserts dispatched_by resolves to a declared mediator row; hub_legacy is declared, and the documented speaker/listener route is untouched, so the suite passes.

baseline.artifact: prototype/mediator_baseline.py sha256:863b8c04a045b7571242b172540e0ba172aece8df9071ba37dd0263460b456d3 (frozen per-arrow suite: hub/party/dispatch range assertions plus the documented-route table; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: 'the interaction is dispatched by the one declared mediator' as a range claim
expressibility_gap.why: with a second mediator declared, range is satisfied by hub_legacy; only the composed-path equations object. The model cannot state that the Mediator object should have one row (that is schema-level, not a finding), so the fault is expressible only because the equation compares derived hubs

discrepancies: Both equations fire on the same row for one fault: eq0 (listener side) and eq1 (speaker side) are distinct witnesses but the same interaction-level report. Element deduplication in the comparison rule keeps the unique set at one row.
procedure: 1. The law was named before any fixture was written (README: dispatch coherence `dispatched_by = participant ; hub`; exclusivity and absence named as the discovery-only and inexpressible halves). The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/mediator/ (README.md, faults.json) before the recorded run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/mediator_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: per-arrow assertions over every row (colleague hub declared; interaction parties declared and distinct; dispatch declared; documented route matched). It never composes two arrows and never asserts a specific mediator row.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, plus `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 2 --json` where the discovery question belongs to the entry.

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements (<object>:<name>); unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings are questions, recorded verbatim and never counted as detections.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; non-empty unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
